world.title: Rubio denies U.S. helped Brazilian senator flee; Trump says he can stay
world.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Oct. 31 that the Trump administration did not help Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro leave Brazil after his defeat in the Oct. 25 presidential runoff. President Donald Trump said Bolsonaro could remain in the United States “as long as he wants”. Rubio said Trump had allowed Bol
world.content: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Oct. 31 that the Trump administration did not help Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro leave Brazil after his defeat in the Oct. 25 presidential runoff. President Donald Trump said Bolsonaro could remain in the United States “as long as he wants”. Rubio said Trump had allowed Bolsonaro to enter because he already had a visa. Bolsonaro arrived in Miami with his family on Oct. 28 after a Brazilian court ordered him to surrender his passports amid investigations into alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion. Brazilian and Indian publications cited reports that Trump adviser Jason Miller helped arrange the private flight, while Rubio denied direct U.S. government involvement. Bolsonaro entered under humanitarian parole, typically a one-year status, and Trump said he had no plans to meet him. Rubio said he expected to meet Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira in France in November.

world.title: US reviews Turkey, India proposals for Black Sea shipping truce
world.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington is reviewing proposals from Turkey and India for a limited Black Sea ceasefire to protect Russian and Ukrainian grain and energy shipments, while pursuing a broader negotiated end to the war. Rubio said the partial ceasefire would not end the conflict, now in its fift
world.content: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington is reviewing proposals from Turkey and India for a limited Black Sea ceasefire to protect Russian and Ukrainian grain and energy shipments, while pursuing a broader negotiated end to the war. Rubio said the partial ceasefire would not end the conflict, now in its fifth year, but could address threats to food and energy security. The G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta ended without a joint statement or agreement. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said talks should also seek a halt to attacks on Ukraine’s electricity and energy infrastructure before winter. She said Ukraine was engaged but Russia had not shown it was ready to proceed. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan called attacks on civilian ships unacceptable after meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Istanbul, while Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Moscow’s position on the war had not changed.

world.title: Yemeni UN staffer dies in Houthi custody; UN demands probe
world.summary: Mohammad el-Shami, a Yemeni staff member of the U.N. Human Rights Office who had been detained since June 6, 2024, died in Houthi custody, the United Nations said Oct. 31. His family was told of his death more than a month after it occurred and has received no explanation of its cause or circumstances, U.N. High Commis
world.content: Mohammad el-Shami, a Yemeni staff member of the U.N. Human Rights Office who had been detained since June 6, 2024, died in Houthi custody, the United Nations said Oct. 31. His family was told of his death more than a month after it occurred and has received no explanation of its cause or circumstances, U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said. Türk called for an independent investigation and the immediate, unconditional release of other detained U.N. personnel, including seven colleagues from his office. U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres also called for an investigation. Yemeni Human Rights Minister Mashdal Mohammed Omar said the Houthis were responsible and that the family had been denied contact with el-Shami and had not received his body. The Houthis made no immediate comment. They have previously said those detained were part of a spy network working for the United States and Israel.
world.image_alt: Yemeni UN staffer dies in Houthi custody; UN demands probe

world.title: Israeli protesters urge alliance with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu after deadlock
world.summary: Thousands of Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv and other cities on Oct. 31, urging opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to work with Arab-led parties to form a government and replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Oct. 27 election left Netanyahu’s bloc with 53 seats, Jewish-led opposition parties with 48 and Arab-led par
world.content: Thousands of Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv and other cities on Oct. 31, urging opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to work with Arab-led parties to form a government and replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Oct. 27 election left Netanyahu’s bloc with 53 seats, Jewish-led opposition parties with 48 and Arab-led parties with 19 in the 120-seat Knesset. A partnership between the opposition and Arab factions could command 67 seats, exceeding the 61 needed for a majority. Eisenkot has not committed to such an arrangement and says prospective partners must recognize Israel as a Jewish, democratic and liberal state and Hamas as a terrorist organization. Several opposition parties have rejected relying on Arab lawmakers, while the Joint List says it is prepared to support an alternative government without joining it. Netanyahu has alleged election fraud and improper foreign support for Arab parties; the Central Elections Committee said its inquiry was limited and would not affect the results. President Isaac Herzog is expected to begin consultations with party leaders this week and designate a candidate to form a government. The Knesset is due to be sworn in on Nov. 10. The designated candidate will have 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to assemble a coalition.
world.image_alt: Israeli protesters urge alliance with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu after deadlock

world.title: India’s opposition demands poll chief’s resignation over voter-roll cuts
world.summary: Tens of thousands of people gathered at New Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday for a rally by the opposition INDIA bloc, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a nationwide voter-roll revision. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi led a march to the venue, where the opposition accused the Ele
world.content: Tens of thousands of people gathered at New Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday for a rally by the opposition INDIA bloc, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a nationwide voter-roll revision. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi led a march to the venue, where the opposition accused the Election Commission of removing eligible voters from the rolls. The commission and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) deny wrongdoing. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which began last year, removed about 130 million names from draft electoral rolls. Opposition parties say the deletions disproportionately affect Muslim and other minority voters and could benefit the BJP. The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove entries for people who have died or moved, as well as duplicate entries. The rally followed a symbolic opposition “impeachment” of Kumar on Saturday that carries no legal force. The commission says voters wrongly removed from the rolls can re-enrol. Under India’s constitution, removing the chief election commissioner requires a formal parliamentary process and a special majority.

world.title: U.S. warns Russia of mass-casualty threat at Moscow palace
world.summary: The U.S. Embassy in Moscow warned on Oct. 31, 2026, of a “credible threat of a mass casualty event” at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, a palace and park complex in southern Moscow, and said Washington was coordinating with Russian authorities. The warning named the site and date but gave no public details about a suspec
world.content: The U.S. Embassy in Moscow warned on Oct. 31, 2026, of a “credible threat of a mass casualty event” at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, a palace and park complex in southern Moscow, and said Washington was coordinating with Russian authorities. The warning named the site and date but gave no public details about a suspected attacker or method. Russia’s Federal Security Service, or FSB, said it had received U.S. information about preparations for an attack through established cooperation channels and was taking appropriate measures. The museum grounds were temporarily closed and access restricted; reports also said visitors were evacuated during a concert at the venue. The U.S. issued a warning in March 2024, days before gunmen attacked Crocus City Hall outside Moscow, killing more than 140 people. As of the latest reports, neither U.S. nor Russian authorities had publicly identified suspects or explained how an attack might be carried out.
world.image_alt: U.S. warns Russia of mass-casualty threat at Moscow palace

world.title: Trump says U.S. may strike remaining Iran targets; Tehran warns of retaliation
world.summary: President Donald Trump said Oct. 31 that the United States may strike one or two remaining targets in Iran, naming the suspected underground nuclear complex at Pickaxe Mountain. Iran’s government denies conducting nuclear work there. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned that any new U.S. or Israeli attack woul
world.content: President Donald Trump said Oct. 31 that the United States may strike one or two remaining targets in Iran, naming the suspected underground nuclear complex at Pickaxe Mountain. Iran’s government denies conducting nuclear work there. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned that any new U.S. or Israeli attack would draw an immediate response without geographic limits, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not decided whether to launch further strikes and Washington remained open to diplomacy. The war began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28. Iran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and the disruption has driven up global energy prices. Qatar and Pakistan are mediating, and Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said there were no plans for direct talks with U.S. officials. The sides remain far apart on terms for ending the conflict, including Iran’s demand for the release of frozen assets. The United States holds midterm elections on Nov. 3, and Gulf officials told MS NOW they had been warned of possible U.S. strikes as early as Nov. 4. Rubio said no decision had been made.

world.title: London police arrest 139 at protest against Palestine Action ban
world.summary: London police arrested 139 people on Oct. 31 at a protest outside the U.S. Embassy in support of Palestine Action, the banned pro-Palestinian direct-action group. The Metropolitan Police said most were detained for expressing support for a proscribed organization and that arrests were continuing. Organizers estimated a
world.content: London police arrested 139 people on Oct. 31 at a protest outside the U.S. Embassy in support of Palestine Action, the banned pro-Palestinian direct-action group. The Metropolitan Police said most were detained for expressing support for a proscribed organization and that arrests were continuing. Organizers estimated about 400 people attended. Defend Our Juries organized the protest ahead of a Nov. 4 Supreme Court hearing on Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori’s challenge to the ban. The government outlawed the group under terrorism legislation in July 2025, making membership or support a criminal offense punishable by up to 14 years in prison. The Court of Appeal overturned a High Court ruling against the ban and upheld the proscription in June 2026. A separate vigil took place outside the U.S. Consulate in Edinburgh. Police Scotland reported no arrests but said it was reviewing evidence and could take further action. In August 2026, the U.S. announced sanctions against Palestine Action and designated it as a terror group.
world.image_alt: London police arrest 139 at protest against Palestine Action ban

business.title: Anthropic reportedly seeks up to $100 billion in IPO at a valuation of up to $2 trillion
business.summary: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, filed for an initial public offering with U.S. regulators on Oct. 26, reporting $16.3 billion in revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss for the first half of 2026. The reported offering could raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2
business.content: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, filed for an initial public offering with U.S. regulators on Oct. 26, reporting $16.3 billion in revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss for the first half of 2026. The reported offering could raise as much as $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, though those figures are estimates rather than final terms. Anthropic has about $417 billion in future minimum computing commitments and expects to add more capacity, while much of its customer revenue depends on usage rather than long-term contracts. The company reportedly plans to begin investor presentations in the second week of November and aims to list before Thanksgiving, Nov. 26.

business.title: UK charity shops face closures as online resale and costs squeeze profits
business.summary: The British Heart Foundation (BHF) plans to close 150 shops after its retail arm lost £3.3 million, while Oxfam’s retail profit fell 23% to £4.9 million in its latest financial year. Cancer Research UK and Scope have also shut or are closing stores. Shoppers increasingly sell better-quality clothes through platforms su
business.content: The British Heart Foundation (BHF) plans to close 150 shops after its retail arm lost £3.3 million, while Oxfam’s retail profit fell 23% to £4.9 million in its latest financial year. Cancer Research UK and Scope have also shut or are closing stores. Shoppers increasingly sell better-quality clothes through platforms such as Vinted and Depop, while charities bear the costs of collecting, sorting and storing donations. UK spending on secondhand clothing has quadrupled to £8.8 billion a year, but charity shops continue to close. BHF aims to shut 90 stores by March 2027 and another 60 by March 2028.
business.image_alt: UK charity shops face closures as online resale and costs squeeze profits

business.title: US judge permanently dismisses Trump’s $10 billion suit against Wall Street Journal
business.summary: U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles on Oct. 31 permanently dismissed President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal, Rupert Murdoch and other defendants, finding that Trump’s amended complaint did not plausibly allege “actual malice”. The case challenged a July 2025 Journal articl
business.content: U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles on Oct. 31 permanently dismissed President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal, Rupert Murdoch and other defendants, finding that Trump’s amended complaint did not plausibly allege “actual malice”. The case challenged a July 2025 Journal article about a sexually suggestive letter bearing Trump’s name in a 2003 album for Jeffrey Epstein’s 50th birthday. Trump denies writing it; Gayles did not decide who wrote the letter. The judge said the Journal had reported Trump’s denial and described its investigation as thoughtful and detailed. He rejected the argument that the paper should have withheld publication after Trump denied the letter’s authenticity, saying that reasoning could let public figures block unfavorable reporting and would conflict with First Amendment protections. Gayles had dismissed an earlier version of the complaint in April but allowed Trump to amend it. Trump filed the amended complaint in May. The dismissal with prejudice bars him from bringing the same claims again in federal court. A spokesman for Trump’s legal team said the president plans to appeal; Dow Jones, the Journal’s publisher, said it was pleased with the ruling.
business.image_alt: US judge permanently dismisses Trump’s $10 billion suit against Wall Street Journal

business.title: Bond investors pause Treasury bets before US midterm vote
business.summary: Bond investors are holding off on new U.S. Treasury positions before Tuesday’s midterm elections, which could shift control of Congress and influence federal spending and oversight of artificial intelligence investment. The pause follows recent bond buying as investors sought to lock in higher yields. Large fund manage
business.content: Bond investors are holding off on new U.S. Treasury positions before Tuesday’s midterm elections, which could shift control of Congress and influence federal spending and oversight of artificial intelligence investment. The pause follows recent bond buying as investors sought to lock in higher yields. Large fund managers are weighing election uncertainty alongside upcoming economic data and Treasury announcements. Investors are also reassessing AI investments after weaker-than-expected third-quarter results from Alphabet and Amazon and disclosures of continued heavy funding needs for data centers. The Nasdaq 100 entered correction territory on Friday. Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s Vishal Khanduja said his team was waiting for the results and new data rather than betting on interest rates based on a single election outcome. The U.S. Treasury’s refunding announcement is due Wednesday, Nov. 4, followed by an inflation reading on Nov. 10.
business.image_alt: Bond investors pause Treasury bets before US midterm vote

business.title: California voters weigh billionaire tax as economists urge property-tax overhaul
business.summary: California voters will decide Proposition 40 on Nov. 3, a proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires’ assets to help fund health care after federal cuts. Economists Owen Zidar of Princeton and Eric Zwick of the University of Chicago argue that changing the state’s property-tax system would provide a broader, more reliabl
business.content: California voters will decide Proposition 40 on Nov. 3, a proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires’ assets to help fund health care after federal cuts. Economists Owen Zidar of Princeton and Eric Zwick of the University of Chicago argue that changing the state’s property-tax system would provide a broader, more reliable revenue base than taxing a small group of billionaires. Opponents warn the wealth tax could prompt wealthy residents and businesses to leave, while California sports-industry figures say teams and fans could bear some of the costs. Tax law professor David Gamage argues that the measure could instead reduce health-care costs and that the effects of federal funding cuts would outweigh possible increases in game-day prices.
business.image_alt: California voters weigh billionaire tax as economists urge property-tax overhaul

business.title: Investors weigh dividend stocks as midterms test prediction markets
business.summary: Investors are assessing whether the U.S. midterm elections will shift market leadership toward dividend stocks, while prediction-market companies face scrutiny over their election forecasts ahead of Tuesday’s vote. Seeking Alpha argues that political uncertainty and potentially lower long-term interest rates could favo
business.content: Investors are assessing whether the U.S. midterm elections will shift market leadership toward dividend stocks, while prediction-market companies face scrutiny over their election forecasts ahead of Tuesday’s vote. Seeking Alpha argues that political uncertainty and potentially lower long-term interest rates could favor dividend-paying shares over artificial intelligence-focused growth stocks. It says the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF, known as SCHD, is up nearly 30% this year. Tarek Mansour, chief executive of prediction-market company Kalshi, said the markets gave a better forecast than public polls. The Wall Street Journal cited recent election surprises in Brazil, Serbia and Wisconsin, and uncertainty over Israel’s next prime minister, ahead of the U.S. midterms.
business.image_alt: Investors weigh dividend stocks as midterms test prediction markets

business.title: Companies deploy AI agents while retaining human checks and oversight
business.summary: South Korean telecommunications company SK Telecom is expanding its company-wide AI program after more than 4,000 employees built agents and 1,500 agents saw regular use under its earlier initiative. The new phase aims to redesign work and collaboration around AI, including experiments pairing employees with agents on
business.content: South Korean telecommunications company SK Telecom is expanding its company-wide AI program after more than 4,000 employees built agents and 1,500 agents saw regular use under its earlier initiative. The new phase aims to redesign work and collaboration around AI, including experiments pairing employees with agents on product development. Other companies are also using agents for business tasks, but the technology still struggles with phone calls and complex real-world work, prompting startups to hand some tasks to human contractors. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said his bank would block unvetted outside agents, while James Comer, chairman of the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, asked Delaware’s governor for documents on a proposed AI-run corporate structure. SK Telecom is extending its experiments across the organization and developing security and data systems to support the expansion.
business.image_alt: Companies deploy AI agents while retaining human checks and oversight

business.title: French banks lose €39bn as weak economy and political risk weigh
business.summary: France’s three largest listed banks have lost €39 billion in market value since September, as strong quarterly earnings failed to reassure investors concerned about the country’s economy and political uncertainty. The sell-off followed Fitch Ratings’ move to put France’s A+ credit rating on a negative outlook, while of
business.content: France’s three largest listed banks have lost €39 billion in market value since September, as strong quarterly earnings failed to reassure investors concerned about the country’s economy and political uncertainty. The sell-off followed Fitch Ratings’ move to put France’s A+ credit rating on a negative outlook, while official data showed the economy contracted 0.1% in the third quarter. BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole and Société Générale each matched or beat analysts’ earnings expectations, helped by equities trading and higher interest income in French retail banking. But investors sold the shares after Crédit Agricole warned of a slowdown in requests for investment projects in France. Its stock has fallen nearly 20% since early September, while all three banks have underperformed the Euro Stoxx Banks index. The government is seeking parliamentary approval for a 2027 budget intended to reduce the deficit, but it lacks a majority and has said it may use constitutional procedures if talks fail. Investors and bank executives are watching whether slower activity will curb demand for credit and increase loan risks.
business.image_alt: French banks lose €39bn as weak economy and political risk weigh

science.title: NASA seeks commercial firms to extend Hubble’s science life before reentry
science.summary: NASA issued a request for information on Oct. 29 asking commercial companies how they could raise the Hubble Space Telescope’s orbit, service it or guide its eventual disposal. Responses are due by 3 p.m. Eastern time on Nov. 30. Hubble has no propulsion system and is losing altitude because of atmospheric drag. NASA p
science.content: NASA issued a request for information on Oct. 29 asking commercial companies how they could raise the Hubble Space Telescope’s orbit, service it or guide its eventual disposal. Responses are due by 3 p.m. Eastern time on Nov. 30. Hubble has no propulsion system and is losing altitude because of atmospheric drag. NASA projects an uncontrolled atmospheric reentry in 2033 or 2034, so any intervention would need to occur by 2032. The request seeks information, not a commitment to purchase a mission: NASA has allocated no funding for Hubble reboost or servicing. Companies would need to provide and launch a spacecraft, operate the mission and, if applicable, supply a crew, while ensuring they do not harm the telescope. NASA is also seeking options for a controlled end to the observatory’s mission.
science.image_alt: NASA seeks commercial firms to extend Hubble’s science life before reentry

science.title: Ghana warns very strong El Niño could intensify heat and drought
science.summary: Ghana’s Meteorological Agency (GMet) warned on Oct. 30 that a very strong El Niño is building in the Pacific and could bring a hotter, drier dry season across much of Ghana, with heat stress expected to peak in February-April 2027. Citing the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Climate Predict
science.content: Ghana’s Meteorological Agency (GMet) warned on Oct. 30 that a very strong El Niño is building in the Pacific and could bring a hotter, drier dry season across much of Ghana, with heat stress expected to peak in February-April 2027. Citing the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center, GMet put the chance of the event reaching very strong intensity in November-January at 96%. GMet forecasts below-normal rainfall across much of Ghana through December but says localized downpours and flooding remain possible. It says the 2027 rains could be late and weak or above normal, depending in part on El Niño’s evolution and conditions in the Gulf of Guinea. Hydropower risks are greater for the 2027 inflow season, which will affect electricity generation in 2028. GMet said it will update its rainy-season forecasts early next year.
science.image_alt: Ghana warns very strong El Niño could intensify heat and drought

science.title: AI agent selects and injects gene therapy into epileptic mouse brain
science.summary: An AI agent at San Francisco biotech startup Exin Therapeutics chose a gene-therapy candidate and controlled a robotic rig to inject it into the brain of a living mouse with epilepsy, according to the company’s CEO and co-founder, Gabriel Ocana Santero. A veterinary surgeon opened the skull, while the agent selected a
science.content: An AI agent at San Francisco biotech startup Exin Therapeutics chose a gene-therapy candidate and controlled a robotic rig to inject it into the brain of a living mouse with epilepsy, according to the company’s CEO and co-founder, Gabriel Ocana Santero. A veterinary surgeon opened the skull, while the agent selected a treatment from 19 gene-therapy vectors and chose the injection site. Researchers have not yet assessed whether the therapy reduces seizures. The team used human approval checkpoints and an emergency motor shutoff, but a coordinate-system glitch delayed the procedure, which took just over an hour. Separately, AI startup Radical Numerics said a patient received AI-designed bacteriophages to treat a resistant infection. The company has not reported the outcome, and its announcement has not been confirmed in a peer-reviewed study.
science.image_alt: AI agent selects and injects gene therapy into epileptic mouse brain

science.title: Survey finds 39% of British singles use AI for dating
science.summary: A Match Group survey of 3,000 British singles found that 39% had used artificial intelligence for dating, including to seek advice, plan dates, practise conversations and write profiles or messages. Use was higher among Gen Z respondents, at 66%, and millennials, at 53%, according to The Guardian. Some users say chatbo
science.content: A Match Group survey of 3,000 British singles found that 39% had used artificial intelligence for dating, including to seek advice, plan dates, practise conversations and write profiles or messages. Use was higher among Gen Z respondents, at 66%, and millennials, at 53%, according to The Guardian. Some users say chatbots help them assess matches or manage anxiety, while others worry about relying on them. About a third of UK singles said they would end a date if they learned their match had used AI to write messages. Match Group’s head of trust and safety, Yoel Roth, said the company opposes AI assistants communicating with each other on users’ behalf.
science.image_alt: Survey finds 39% of British singles use AI for dating

science.title: Simulations weaken theory that comets delivered life’s building blocks to Earth
science.summary: A team led by University of Cambridge astronomer Richard Anslow found that comet impacts were unlikely to deliver intact hydrogen cyanide, a molecule relevant to prebiotic chemistry, to early Earth, based on 100,000 computer simulations. The models suggest comets generally struck too fast, exposing organic molecules to
science.content: A team led by University of Cambridge astronomer Richard Anslow found that comet impacts were unlikely to deliver intact hydrogen cyanide, a molecule relevant to prebiotic chemistry, to early Earth, based on 100,000 computer simulations. The models suggest comets generally struck too fast, exposing organic molecules to destructive heat and pressure. In 54% of simulations, no impact occurred; the rest produced at least one, but only a tiny minority yielded up to three collisions. The findings do not rule out all comet contributions to life’s ingredients. Earth-science researcher Queenie Chan said chemical reactions before atmospheric entry could have produced more impact-resistant compounds. The study, published in Scientific Reports, also identifies possible alternatives, including asteroids and chemical production on Earth. Anslow said comet impacts on ancient Mars may have been gentler.
science.image_alt: Simulations weaken theory that comets delivered life’s building blocks to Earth

science.title: Cowboy Space pitches Big Iron rocket for orbital AI data centers
science.summary: Cowboy Space has proposed Big Iron, a rocket intended to launch orbital AI data centers, with an upper stage designed to become the satellite itself. The company is targeting a first launch in late 2028, but its nine planned Clydesdale engines have undergone only component testing and are not ready for a test launch. C
science.content: Cowboy Space has proposed Big Iron, a rocket intended to launch orbital AI data centers, with an upper stage designed to become the satellite itself. The company is targeting a first launch in late 2028, but its nine planned Clydesdale engines have undergone only component testing and are not ready for a test launch. Cowboy has conducted one space mission: a test unit called Reason-1 flew on a SpaceX rideshare launch to test components for a possible power-beaming satellite. ExtremeTech questioned the technical and economic viability of orbital data centers, citing heat dissipation and competition with terrestrial data centers.
science.image_alt: Cowboy Space pitches Big Iron rocket for orbital AI data centers

science.title: Researchers favor permanent standard time as US debates clock changes
science.summary: Most U.S. clocks turn back one hour Nov. 1, as new research reviews renew debate over whether year-round standard time or daylight saving time better supports health. A Canadian policy analysis and a review focused on people with mental illness argue that permanent standard time better protects sleep, mood and biologic
science.content: Most U.S. clocks turn back one hour Nov. 1, as new research reviews renew debate over whether year-round standard time or daylight saving time better supports health. A Canadian policy analysis and a review focused on people with mental illness argue that permanent standard time better protects sleep, mood and biological rhythms. A broader review of population studies, however, finds a mix of harms and benefits from seasonal clock changes and summer daylight saving time. Permanent daylight saving time would delay winter sunrise, while permanent standard time would bring earlier summer sunrises and winter sunsets. The U.S. House passed a bill to make daylight saving time permanent in July 2026, but the Senate has not taken it up. The next seasonal clock change is scheduled for March 14, 2027.
science.image_alt: Researchers favor permanent standard time as US debates clock changes

science.title: Study suggests Neptune formed from materials that originated closer to the young Sun
science.summary: Neptune may have formed from building blocks that originated closer to the young Sun before moving outward, according to research published in Astronomy & Astrophysics. Neptune’s deep atmosphere appears considerably richer in oxygen than Uranus’s, despite the planets’ similar size and mass, suggesting different chemica
science.content: Neptune may have formed from building blocks that originated closer to the young Sun before moving outward, according to research published in Astronomy & Astrophysics. Neptune’s deep atmosphere appears considerably richer in oxygen than Uranus’s, despite the planets’ similar size and mass, suggesting different chemical histories. Researchers used carbon monoxide measurements and atmospheric models to infer the planets’ hidden chemistry; they cannot directly sample the deep atmospheres. The proposed formation pathway therefore depends on models. Future spacecraft observations or atmospheric probes could help test it. NASA’s planned Uranus Orbiter and Probe is expected to launch sometime in the next decade.
science.image_alt: Study suggests Neptune formed from materials that originated closer to the young Sun

sports.title: USC defeats No. 2 Ohio State 30-18
sports.summary: Southern California (USC) beat second-ranked Ohio State 30-18 in Los Angeles on Saturday, Oct. 31, improving to 7-2 under coach Lincoln Riley. Freshman receiver Trent Mosley opened the scoring with a 69-yard touchdown catch, and tight end Mark Bowman’s 70-yard catch-and-run helped set up another score. Quarterback Jayd
sports.content: Southern California (USC) beat second-ranked Ohio State 30-18 in Los Angeles on Saturday, Oct. 31, improving to 7-2 under coach Lincoln Riley. Freshman receiver Trent Mosley opened the scoring with a 69-yard touchdown catch, and tight end Mark Bowman’s 70-yard catch-and-run helped set up another score. Quarterback Jayden Maiava passed for 222 yards, while USC’s defense kept Ohio State out of the end zone until the fourth quarter. Ohio State, now 6-2, played without injured starting quarterback Julian Sayin. Freshman Luke Fahey threw for 260 yards in his first career start. The Buckeyes gained 464 yards but managed only one touchdown, with penalties and missed red-zone chances contributing to the loss. USC has three regular-season games left, including matchups with Indiana and unbeaten UCLA. Ohio State has four games remaining.

sports.content: Brentford beat Nottingham Forest 2-0 in London on Saturday, extending Forest’s winless run to five league matches and leaving them 19th with one win from their opening nine games. Nikola Milenkovic turned Dango Ouattara’s cross into his own net before Igor Thiago scored in the 76th minute. The victory ended Brentford’s four-match winless streak. Forest created chances but failed to convert them. Head coach Oliver Glasner said he would change his approach after admitting he had compromised too much. He warned that players must follow his plan or the club could appoint a sixth manager in just over a year. Forest’s next league game is against leaders Manchester City next weekend.

sports.content: Coventry City beat Sunderland 3-1 on Saturday to climb out of the Premier League relegation zone, leaving Sunderland bottom after nine matches. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto opened the scoring in the 17th minute, Taiwo Awoniyi made it 2-0 before half-time and Jack Rudoni added a third early in the second half. Enzo Le Fée converted a penalty for Sunderland, but the visitors could not recover. Defender Omar Alderete was sent off late on. Sunderland have five points and are winless in seven Premier League games, despite winning four of their five cup matches. Head coach Régis Le Bris said the packed schedule was demanding, while captain Granit Xhaka called for the team to show character. Sunderland face Dinamo Zagreb before a league game against Chelsea, then have a difficult run of fixtures before visiting AC Milan on 10 December.

sports.title: Hamilton takes first Ferrari pole, edges Russell by 0.009 seconds

sports.content: Lewis Hamilton took his first Formula 1 Grand Prix pole for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix, clocking 1:16.514 to beat Mercedes’ George Russell by 0.009 seconds. The 41-year-old’s 105th career pole is his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix and Ferrari’s first of the 2026 season. He is the oldest pole-sitter since Mario Andretti in 1982. Hamilton and Russell will start on the front row, with Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc third. Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli qualified fifth but moves up to fourth after Max Verstappen’s grid penalty. Antonelli will secure the title by finishing ninth or higher; if neither Hamilton nor Russell wins, he becomes champion regardless of his own result. The 71-lap race is scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 1, in Mexico City. Hamilton took his first Ferrari victory in Barcelona earlier this season, while Antonelli can clinch his first championship on Sunday.

sports.content: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in San Francisco on Oct. 31 to win their first WNBA championship in only their second season, clinching the first Game 7 in Finals history. Forward Gabby Williams, named Finals MVP, scored 30 points, including a Finals-record 28 in the second half, after Golden State trailed by six at halftime. Williams’ late 31-foot three-pointer put the Valkyries ahead for good, and Kiah Stokes’ putback helped protect the lead. Veronica Burton scored Golden State’s final points at the free-throw line. Atlanta’s Jordin Canada scored 18 points and Allisha Gray added 16. Golden State reached the playoffs in its inaugural season. Atlanta, seeking its first championship in its fourth Finals appearance, lost after forcing the winner-take-all game with an 80-69 Game 6 win.

sports.content: Sovereignty, the four-year-old colt owned by Dubai-based Godolphin, won the $7 million Breeders’ Cup Classic at Keeneland on Oct. 31, beating The Puma by 1¾ lengths. Stablemate Knightsbridge finished third, while defending champion Forever Young was fifth and Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes winner Golden Tempo finished sixth. With jockey Junior Alvarado aboard, Sovereignty passed Knightsbridge in the stretch and completed the 1¼-mile race in 2:00.36. The victory came a year after Sovereignty missed the Classic because of a fever; a foot abscess and an 84-day gap between races also complicated his 2026 campaign. Trainer Bill Mott said the Godolphin team’s decision to keep him in training made his return possible. Sovereignty is expected to retire to stud, and the win is likely to earn him a second consecutive Horse of the Year honor. T O Elvis became the first Japanese-trained horse to win the Breeders’ Cup Sprint. In the $5 million Turf, Irish colt Benvenuto Cellini gave jockey Ryan Moore a record sixth win in the race and trainer Aidan O’Brien his record-extending eighth. O’Brien can pursue a new calendar-year record for top-level wins in Hong Kong in December.

sports.content: Brighton & Hove Albion beat Manchester City 1-0 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, earning their first away league victory there after 18 attempts. Brighton’s Yasin Ayari scored in the 11th minute after City defender Matheus Nunes failed to clear a cross, and Brighton held on to win. City suffered their second straight Premier League defeat after winning their first seven games. Brighton moved to third on 19 points, two behind City on 21; Arsenal could overtake City by avoiding defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen made seven saves as City pressed for an equaliser. The win followed Brighton’s League Cup shootout defeat to City on Wednesday. City next travel to RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.

sports.summary: Northampton Saints recovered from a 14-point deficit to beat Gloucester 28-14 in the Premiership on Saturday, scoring 28 unanswered points at Franklin’s Gardens. sports.content: Northampton Saints recovered from a 14-point deficit to beat Gloucester 28-14 in the Premiership on Saturday, scoring 28 unanswered points at Franklin’s Gardens. Scrum-half Alex Mitchell left after 21 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury, eight days before England’s Nations Championship opener against Australia on Nov. 8. Northampton fly-half Fin Smith and scrum-half Archie McParland both have calf problems, while Mitchell has had recurring hamstring trouble this year. Northampton director of rugby Phil Dowson said the club would be cautious with Mitchell; England head coach Steve Borthwick was due to confirm his squad on Monday. Two driving-maul tries began Northampton’s comeback before late tries from George Hendy and replacement Rory Hutchinson secured the bonus-point win.
